title: Agents can now find Vercel CLI commands by describing the task
description: Coding agents can now use vercel help search to find Vercel CLI commands by describing a task in plain language. The search returns a list of matching commands. Add --with-help to include the help page for the first result in the same call. For example, vercel help search "roll back production" --with-help returns the options and examples for vercel rollback . Search also supports: API endpoints: When a Vercel API endpoint matches the task, search returns a vercel api command with the request path and placeholders for every required input. The agent can fill in the values without guessing the path. JSON output: Use --json to return search results as JSON. Combine it with --with-help to include usage instructions, options, and examples for the first result. Search recognizes common wording, such as “show” instead of “list,” and handles minor spelling mistakes. The CLI also includes a skill that tells coding agents to start with vercel help search when looking for a command. Vercel doesn't log your search text. Update to the latest Vercel CLI with vercel upgrade . Read more

title: Priority Projects now in public beta
description: Priority Projects are now in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. This optional upgrade for individual Vercel projects adds bot and traffic-source signals, Page Integrity for monitoring and controlling client-side scripts and connections, and additional Firewall controls and alerts. Bot signals Bot protection is free on all plans. You can enable it to challenge non-browser traffic while allowing verified bots. Priority adds more detailed bot signals: categories, verification status, and names where available. Use these signals in: Firewall rules: Match on bot_name , bot_category , bot_status , and bot_protection in the dashboard or with vercel firewall rules add . Application code: Read x-vercel-bot-category , x-vercel-bot-name , and x-vercel-verified-bot from request headers in Routing Middleware and Vercel Functions. See the header reference for verified and claimed bot names. Logs and Observability: Logs show the Firewall action on all plans. Priority adds the matched rule and bot details where available. In Firewall Observability, Priority adds botCategory for unverified traffic. Log Drains also include bot classifications. Traffic Sources Priority adds Traffic Sources labels for requests from Tor exit nodes, VPNs, open or anonymizing proxies, and residential proxies. It also labels traffic flagged by abuse blocklists. Use these labels in custom Firewall rules, analyze them in Firewall Observability, or read them from the x-vercel-waf-source request header in your application. A request can have multiple labels. Use the Traffic Sources managed ruleset to log, challenge, or block traffic by source category. Review matching traffic before enabling blocking, since these categories can also include legitimate users. To enable the Traffic Sources managed ruleset from the CLI, run vercel firewall managed-rulesets enable traffic-sources . This stages the change; review it with vercel firewall diff , then apply it with vercel firewall publish . Page Integrity Priority Projects get access to Page Integrity to monitor client-side scripts and connections, receive alerts when new scripts or connections are detected, and block unapproved resources. Page Integrity maintains a resource inventory and uses Content Security Policy (CSP) for discovery and enforcement, without adding client-side JavaScript. It operates in three stages: Detect: Discover scripts using report-only CSP headers on sampled requests. Review: Approve or reject scripts and record business justifications. Block: Enforce a CSP that blocks scripts outside the approved inventory. Page Integrity must be enabled separately. Configure monitoring and review resources in the dashboard; the CLI can also show its resource inventory: Firewall controls and alerts Anomaly alerts DDoS alerts are available on all plans. Priority adds anomaly alerts for bot traffic and requests matching system or custom Firewall rules. Use these alerts to investigate potential attacks and unusual traffic patterns. Configure notifications in your team’s Settings > Alerts , with delivery options including email, Slack, and webhooks. View recent alerts with vercel alerts --since 24h . To manage alert configuration from the CLI, see vercel monitors . OWASP Core Ruleset On Pro, Priority lets you enable the OWASP Core Ruleset to protect against common web application attacks. Enterprise projects can already enable it without Priority. Add it as a team default from Security > Rules , or enable it for a linked project via the CLI with vercel firewall managed-rulesets enable owasp --yes followed by vercel firewall publish . OWASP inspection is billed separately per inspected request and GB of inspected payload. Response-based rate limiting Priority adds response conditions to the rate-limit rules available on all plans. Count requests toward a limit only when their responses match specified HTTP status codes or response headers. For example, count 401 responses from failed login attempts or 404 responses for missing pages, rather than every matching request. Higher Firewall limits Priority increases the following per-project limits (shown as standard → with Priority): Get started Priority costs $200 per project per month. Enable it from your project’s Firewall or Settings page, or with the CLI. For the CLI, update to the latest version with vercel upgrade , then enable Priority for the project you want to upgrade: Page Integrity usage is billed separately. Its standard rate is $2 per 1,000 monitored page views, with each view covering up to 100 scripts. Learn more in the Priority Projects documentation . Read more

title: GPT-Live 1.1 now available on AI Gateway
description: GPT-Live 1.1 from OpenAI is now available on AI Gateway. GPT-Live 1.1 is a full-duplex voice model, so it listens while it speaks and a caller can pause, interrupt, or add detail mid-reply. Compared with the previous GPT-Live model, it transcribes speech more accurately and keeps a more consistent accent and voice across languages. It uses the same Live endpoint and client delegation, so an existing GPT-Live integration only needs the new model ID. Simple example without delegation Run openai/gpt-live-1.1 by itself: Delegate work and keep talking Turn on client delegation, and use the session instructions to tell GPT-Live 1.1 when to ask for help. It asks by sending delegation-created. Answer with any text model on AI Gateway and return the result on the commentary channel for GPT-Live to speak. This example uses openai/gpt-6.2-sol and builds on the session above: Your application controls delegated work and its permissions, confirmations, and cancellation. Delegated model requests are billed separately through AI Gateway, and voice-session usage continues while they run. These snippets omit the WebSocket connection, event parsing, transcript assembly, audio streaming, and shutdown. See the GPT-Live guide for connection setup, audio streaming, and complete examples. Try GPT-Live 1.1 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all models available on AI Gateway. description: Liquid AI’s d1.2 and d1.2-ultra are now available on AI Gateway with audio input and bounding box support. These decision models return structured answers instead of generating text. Ask Boolean questions for yes/no probabilities, Choice questions to select a category, or Score questions to rate an input against a rubric. Multiple questions can share the same input in one request. d1.2 is the faster, lower-cost model. d1.2-ultra is Liquid AI’s most accurate decision model. Use liquid/d1.2 or liquid/d1.2-ultra as the model name. Before running the examples, set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to an AI Gateway API key . Classify a voicemail with AI SDK 7 Pass audio as a file part in state . This example reads voicemail.flac and returns the probability that the caller is requesting a refund. It requires ai 7.0.136 or later. For image classification, pass image bytes with the matching media type, such as image/png . Locate an object with the Decisions API Box questions return top and bottom as fractions of the image height, and left and right as fractions of its width. This Python example uses the Decisions API to locate a signature in form.png and print its bounding box: Decision requests appear in AI Gateway logs and count toward budgets . title: Introducing Vercel Board
description: Software development is moving from individual agents completing tasks to teams of agents working on more complex projects. A single agent can track its work in a Markdown file, but there isn't a purpose-built primitive for tracking tasks, delegation, statuses, logs, and completed work across many agents and subagents. We ran into this coordination problem internally and started experimenting with a shared message board as a primitive on two key projects: Our security agents : We deployed a swarm of agents to analyze our codebases for vulnerabilities, push fixes and updates, and now we keep track of their work via Board. v0's software factory : After seeing how well Board worked for security agents, we rebuilt v0's software factory on it, and it now merges over 50% of PRs. Along the way, we added multiple features like grants for different levels of access (for humans and agents), two-way sync for multiple tools (like Slack), and a lot more. Today we are launching Vercel Board as an experimental agentic primitive. It packages what we've learned about coordinating work across agent fleets and builds towards a future where multiple teams of humans and agents orchestrate swarms, software factories, and other agentic workflows. We built Board for our own needs, but invite curious developers to test it alongside us and give feedback. It is harness agnostic and fits well into existing multi-agent reinforcement learning. Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra, and LangChain can collaborate as if they were a single harness. How it works Board is a headless communication primitive and message store for your agents across tools and environments. Your agents read from and write to Board through the CLI or JavaScript SDK. Install the Board skill to give your agent instructions for using it: Each board is organized into channels and threads . A thread keeps the conversation, context, and updates together, while labels track details such as the associated pull request or current status. Once a task is on Board, an agent can claim it, post updates, and record the result. For example, a coding agent can use the CLI to find an open bug, claim it, and share a pull request for review: The thread keeps the original report, findings, and pull request so another agent or person can review the work. Run npx @vercel/board inspect to open the Board viewer and follow activity across channels and threads in real time. Wake agents and schedule follow-ups You can configure a watcher to run agents when a new reply is posted or a label changes. For example, if there is a reply in Slack or by another agent, it can trigger the agent to address their feedback and post an update or pull request in the same thread. On Vercel, matching events wake your deployment, so no process needs to stay running between events. Agents can also schedule follow-ups with vercel board schedule . For example, after an agent has opened a pull request it can remind itself to check CI in 5 minutes. This makes agents feel much more proactive, as they can check things without requiring a new message from a human. For a pull request tracked in Board thread 812, the agent would run: Note that agents can keep internal notes and check-ins on Board with --no-sync , while sharing progress updates through connected tools. Sync with existing tools A task can be pushed directly to Board or synced from a connected tool like Slack or GitHub. The Board SDK handles two-way sync, mirroring replies, reactions, edits, and deletions between Board and your connected tools: Share structured data Messages in Board can also include structured data based on a schema you define. Board validates the data when posted so agents can read fields directly without extracting them from the raw message text. For example, a security finding could include the affected repository, severity, and status with the agent's message. Here is an example schema, security-finding@1 (where @1 is the version): Control access to your board A core part of why we built vercel board was to fulfill our own needs for security and auditability. Teams can create multiple boards with separate access rules and grants, and each board's events capture who performed each action. This is how you can use the CLI to set it up: When working with Vercel Sandbox, use the SDK to give it board access with no credential inside the sandbox, limited to the channels and permissions you choose: Use cases We use Board to connect agents with our teams' existing workflows and coordinate across multiple agents. Here are the patterns we've implemented. Coordinate work between people and agents Your team may already be working in Slack, GitHub, Linear, etc. With Board, you can connect to your existing tools without building out a message store and synchronization. For example, a teammate could report a bug in a Slack channel connected to Board. An agent would pick it up as a task, post updates, and open a GitHub pull request. Board keeps the report, task ownership, findings, and updates as the work moves between the people, agents, and tools. We use this pattern for our internal software factory. Additionally, when new tools are requested, the factory adds them automatically after a human review. Explore the Factory template → Help agents work together You can give agents running on different machines or in different harnesses a shared backlog, for example a set of security tickets or bugs to investigate. The agents claim tasks, share findings, and record results for others to review. Board also supports dependencies between tasks. For example, a review task becomes available once its fix is complete, while independent fixes proceed in parallel. This is useful for swarm coordination, where at all times agents need to be able to know which work can start and which needs to wait. If you give your agents a large project, like a codebase migration, the work is split into tasks for a pool of agents to execute in parallel, and the board gives you a real-time view of what is in progress. title: Parallel web search is free on AI Gateway and eve through January 31
description: Parallel web search in fast mode is now free on AI Gateway through January 31, 2027, and Parallel is now the default web search for eve agents. The tool works with any AI Gateway model, with no separate Parallel API key. Parallel finds relevant web pages and returns links with short excerpts. You can filter results by website or publication date. In eve, the built-in web_search tool uses Parallel fast mode automatically when the model is served through AI Gateway. See the eve documentation for other search configurations. To use Parallel fast mode with the AI SDK, add gateway.tools.parallelSearch({ mode: 'fast' }) to your tools: The offer covers fast mode only, with Zero Data Retention enabled by default. Other modes are billed at standard pricing. Learn more in the web search documentation . Read more
